scenes.tts: How can a small graft make its host build a second spinal cord, from cells meant for skin?
scenes.visual: Title card: One Sheet, Two Fates. Two newt larvae side by side; one has a second back and a second neural tube along its flank.
scenes.narration: How can a small graft make its host build a second spinal cord, from cells meant for skin?

scenes.tts: First, a little embryology. The egg divides into a ball of smaller cells.
scenes.visual: A fertilized egg cleaves into 2, 4, 8 cells, then a ball of many small cells, without growing. Label: cleavage.
scenes.narration: First, a little embryology. The egg divides into a ball of smaller cells.

scenes.tts: In amphibians, the ball becomes a blastula, a sphere of cells around a fluid-filled cavity.
scenes.visual: The ball cut in half shows a cavity inside a wall of cells. Label: blastula.
scenes.narration: In amphibians, the ball becomes a blastula, a sphere of cells around a fluid-filled cavity.

scenes.tts: Then, in gastrulation, cells move inside, and the embryo sorts into three layers.
scenes.visual: Cells on the surface stream inward. Three colour bands appear: outer, middle, inner. Label: gastrulation.
scenes.narration: Then, in gastrulation, cells move inside, and the embryo sorts into three layers.

scenes.tts: The outer layer, the ectoderm, makes the outer skin and the nervous system.
scenes.visual: Outer band highlighted, labelled ectoderm, with icons for skin and for brain and spinal cord.
scenes.narration: The outer layer, the ectoderm, makes the outer skin and the nervous system.

scenes.tts: The middle layer, the mesoderm, makes muscle, bone and the notochord, a stiff rod along the back. The inner layer lines the gut.
scenes.visual: Middle band labelled mesoderm, with icons for muscle, bone and a rod labelled notochord. Inner band labelled endoderm, lining a gut tube.
scenes.narration: The middle layer, the mesoderm, makes muscle, bone and the notochord, a stiff rod along the back. The inner layer lines the gut.

scenes.tts: Cells move inside through a slit, the blastopore. Its edge on the future back is the dorsal lip.
scenes.visual: A gastrula with a short curved groove on one side, labelled blastopore; its upper edge glows, labelled dorsal lip. Arrow: future back.
scenes.narration: Cells move inside through a slit, the blastopore. Its edge on the future back is the dorsal lip.

scenes.tts: Now watch the ectoderm. It looks like one sheet.
scenes.visual: A gastrula cut in half; the outer sheet drawn as one layer with a faint tint, no regions marked.
scenes.narration: Now watch the ectoderm. It looks like one sheet.

scenes.tts: Along the back, a strip becomes the neural plate. It rolls up into the neural tube, the future brain and spinal cord.
scenes.visual: Time-lapse: the back strip thickens (label: neural plate), its edges rise, fold and meet as a tube (label: neural tube).
scenes.narration: Along the back, a strip becomes the neural plate. It rolls up into the neural tube, the future brain and spinal cord.

scenes.tts: On the belly, the same sheet stays flat and becomes skin.
scenes.visual: Split view: back strip rolled into a tube; belly sheet flat, labelled skin.
scenes.narration: On the belly, the same sheet stays flat and becomes skin.

scenes.tts: So why does the back strip become neural, while the belly strip becomes skin?
scenes.visual: On screen: Why does the back strip become neural, and the belly become skin?
scenes.narration: So why does the back strip become neural, while the belly strip becomes skin?

scenes.tts: There are two kinds of answer. Perhaps the belly cells are already fixed as skin.
scenes.visual: Card, answer 1: belly cells already fixed as skin, whatever lies next to them.
scenes.narration: There are two kinds of answer. Perhaps the belly cells are already fixed as skin.

scenes.tts: Or they can still change, and something nearby tells the back strip what to become.
scenes.visual: Card, answer 2: the cells can still change. An arrow from nearby tissue points at the back strip.
scenes.narration: Or they can still change, and something nearby tells the back strip what to become.

scenes.tts: Moving tissue tests the first answer. Put dorsal-lip tissue next to belly ectoderm, and watch.
scenes.visual: A dorsal-lip piece is lifted and placed against belly ectoderm. Question mark over the belly.
scenes.narration: Moving tissue tests the first answer. Put dorsal-lip tissue next to belly ectoderm, and watch.

scenes.tts: The graft worked. The belly cells built a second neural tube. Chapter two shows whose cells they were.
scenes.visual: The question mark over the belly resolves: a second neural tube rises at the graft site. Caption: Whose cells? Chapter two.
scenes.narration: The graft worked. The belly cells built a second neural tube. Chapter two shows whose cells they were.

scenes.tts: That experiment gives this lesson its one idea.
scenes.visual: Card: The one idea to carry through this lesson.
scenes.narration: That experiment gives this lesson its one idea.

scenes.tts: A cell's fate can be set by its neighbours.
scenes.visual: The idea builds on screen, line 1: A cell's fate can be set by its neighbours.
scenes.narration: A cell's fate can be set by its neighbours.

scenes.tts: Move the organizer somewhere new, and host cells there build much of a second back around it. The graft itself becomes notochord.
scenes.visual: Line 2 appears: Move the organizer somewhere new, and host cells there build much of a second back around it (the graft itself becomes notochord).
scenes.narration: Move the organizer somewhere new, and host cells there build much of a second back around it. The graft itself becomes notochord.

scenes.tts: But only while they are still competent, that is, able to answer.
scenes.visual: Line 3 appears: but only while they are still competent, able to answer.
scenes.narration: But only while they are still competent, that is, able to answer.

scenes.tts: Notice one limit. The idea says who changed fate, and where. Not what the signal is.
scenes.visual: Limits card: who and where, not what.
scenes.narration: Notice one limit. The idea says who changed fate, and where. Not what the signal is.

scenes.tts: One sheet, two fates, and neighbours can decide which. Next: whose cells built the second back?
scenes.visual: Closing card: One sheet, two fates. Next: Whose cells built it?
scenes.narration: One sheet, two fates, and neighbours can decide which. Next: whose cells built the second back?
